role: AK_TEXT (the printed witness of al-Khwarizmi's treatise)
comment: PDF 3, printed p. 2: the beginning of the treatise: the basmala; the duty of the wise to keep the customs of the righteous; the Torah on the lights as signs for times, days and years (Genesis 1:14); the command to keep the month of the flowers, Nisan, and the Passover on its fifteenth night, at the full moon (de Blois's section 1).

observations: The running head «استخراج تاريخ اليهود للخوارزمى» stands at the head of the page, the page number «٢» at its right; at the lower left the catchword «وابتلاء», the first word of p. 3 (PDF 4); recorded here, not transcribed as lines. L01, the basmala, is centred; L05 begins with a paragraph indent. L04 ends with the edition's full stop, a large round dot at mid-height, written •.

Spacing. The edition sets the letters that do not join the next with irregular white after them: on this page the white inside a word after such a letter measures 5 to 14 px (العا قل, الصا لحين, ذ لك 13 px), and a word space 6 to 17 px (calendar/tools/gaps.py), so that the gaps do not show where a word ends. The words are divided by the sense. Where the print suggests another division: L03, the alif of اذا stands 7 px from فعل and 14 px from the ذ, so that the line reads at first sight «فاذ افعل»; L06, «والنهار ودليلا» is set «والنها رود ليلا» (13 px after the alif, 15 px after the د), and «ليلا على» with 6 px between the words.

Read as printed: L02 «مفترض»; L04 «بالمؤونة», with the hamza on the first و, «والآخرة» with the madda; L08 «الموكد» without hamza, «الاوراد», «نيسن»; L11 «فسحا», the Passover, with س; L13 «رأس» with the hamza; L14 «آى» with the madda and the final ى without dots; L15 «التورٰة», with a small raised alif in place of the alif of التوراة (so printed with the full alif in L05). L14: the two dots of the ي of «كثيرة» run into the tail of the ر; L06: those of «والايام» stand low under the line.
In the left margin beside L06, a short vertical stroke (about 25 px), outside the text block; not transcribed.

critical_notes.evidence: the quotation is Genesis 1:14, «Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years» (Hebrew yehi meʾorot birqiaʿ ha-shamayim); the sentence needs the verb «let there be», لتكن; «لكن», «but», gives no sense before «الصبا فى ربيع فصلا بين الليل والنهار»
«the firmament» of Genesis 1:14 is Hebrew raqiaʿ, which Arabic versions of the Bible keep as رقيع; «ربيع», «spring», gives no sense here; ب and ق differ only in their dots

Genesis 1:14 has «lights» (Hebrew meʾorot) as the subject that divides the day from the night; «الصبا» (the east wind; youth) gives no sense; الضيا(ء), «the light», differs from it only in the dots of ض and ي; another word for the lights is possible
